\[
\mathbf{r}(t) = \mathbf{R} + t\mathbf{d}
\]

where \(\mathbf{R}\) is the position vector at \( t = 0 \), and \(\mathbf{d}\) is the direction vector of the line.

First, we find the direction vector \(\mathbf{d}\). The direction vector \(\mathbf{d}\) can be obtained by subtracting the value of the position vector at \( t = 2 \) from the value of the position vector at \( t = 3 \):

\[
\mathbf{d} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 - 1 \\ -4 - 4 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -8 \end{pmatrix}
\]

So, the parametric equation of the line is:

\[
\mathbf{r}(t) = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} + (t - 2) \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -8 \end{pmatrix}
\]

To find the vector at \( t = -7 \), we substitute \( t = -7 \) into the parametric equation:

\[
\mathbf{r}(-7) = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} + (-7 - 2) \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -8 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} + (-9) \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -8 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} -18 \\ 72 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 - 18 \\ 4 + 72 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -17 \\ 76 \end{pmatrix}
\]

Therefore, the vector on the line at \( t = -7 \) is:

\[
\boxed{\begin{pmatrix} -17 \\ 76 \end{pmatrix}}
\]
